# # Map customer tonic gRPC client stream stuck after server cancel to the tonic Streaming / tokio mpsc cancellation boundary

A customer reports that their tonic-based gRPC client occasionally
hangs forever on the next() call of a server-streaming RPC after the
server explicitly cancels the stream with Status::cancelled(). The
underlying HTTP/2 RST_STREAM is observed in tcpdump, but the
Streaming<T> never returns None.

Your task:
1. Find where tonic's Streaming type wraps the inner mpsc channel
   and how it converts a Status::cancelled into a stream end.
2. Find where tokio's mpsc Receiver decides between Some(item) and
   None on a closed channel, and how it interacts with sender drop
   ordering.
3. Trace the cross-repo path: tonic Streaming::poll_next -> mpsc
   Receiver::poll_recv -> server-side Status::cancelled emit ->
   sender drop -> Receiver close. Cite each file and the function
   responsible.
4. Identify why a Status::cancelled body frame on the wire does
   not always close tonic's mpsc sender immediately when h2 stream
   reset arrives at the client, and how an outstanding clone of
   the sender keeps the client receiver hanging.


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0, github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0

Now I have the complete picture. Here is the full trace and root-cause analysis.

---

## Complete trace and root-cause

### 1. `Streaming<T>` internals — how it wraps the HTTP body

`Streaming<T>` is defined in [tonic/src/codec/decode.rs](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L22-L36). It does **not** wrap an mpsc receiver itself; it wraps a `BoxBody` (an erased HTTP/2 body) and a `Decoder`. The mpsc channel is an *application-level* pattern used by server implementations (described below).

Key fields:
```
Streaming<T>
  └─ decoder: Box<dyn Decoder<...>>
  └─ inner: StreamingInner
       └─ body: BoxBody          ← poll_data / poll_trailers
       └─ state: State           ← ReadHeader | ReadBody | Error
       └─ buf: BytesMut
```

#### `poll_next` — [decode.rs L383-L406](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L383-L406)

```rust
fn poll_next(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Self::Item>> {
    loop {
        if let State::Error = &self.inner.state { return Poll::Ready(None); }
        if let Some(item) = self.decode_chunk()? { return Poll::Ready(Some(Ok(item))); }
        match ready!(self.inner.poll_data(cx))? {
            Some(()) => (),
            None => break,                  // body data exhausted
        }
    }
    // After data is exhausted, poll trailers to get final grpc-status
    Poll::Ready(match ready!(self.inner.poll_response(cx)) {
        Ok(()) => None,
        Err(err) => Some(Err(err)),
    })
}
```

The loop: drain buffered bytes → try decoding a message → poll the body for more bytes. When the body yields `None` (data exhausted), it falls through to `poll_response` which calls `poll_trailers`.

#### `poll_data` — [decode.rs L233-L263](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L233-L263)

```rust
fn poll_data(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<Option<()>, Status>> {
    match ready!(Pin::new(&mut self.body).poll_data(cx)) {
        Some(Ok(d))     => { self.buf.put(d); Poll::Ready(Ok(Some(()))) }
        Some(Err(status)) => {
            // *** The Cancelled special-case is only for Direction::Request ***
            if self.direction == Direction::Request && status.code() == Code::Cancelled {
                return Poll::Ready(Ok(None));   // clean end of stream
            }
            let _ = std::mem::replace(&mut self.state, State::Error);
            Poll::Ready(Err(status))
        }
        None => Poll::Ready(Ok(None)),
    }
}
```

**Critical asymmetry:** the `Code::Cancelled` short-circuit only fires for `Direction::Request` (server-side, reading the client's request body). For a **client-side `Direction::Response`** stream — which is the streaming RPC case the customer describes — a cancelled error from the body propagates as `Poll::Ready(Err(status))`, which is then returned as `Some(Err(...))` from `poll_next`, **not** as `None`. The stream never cleanly closes.

The body error arrives via `map_err` installed at construction ([decode.rs L126](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L125-L127)):
```rust
body.map_err(|err| Status::map_error(err.into()))
```
And `Status::map_error` → `Status::from_error` → `Status::try_from_error` → `Status::from_h2_error` ([status.rs L346-L388](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/status.rs?L346-L389)).

The h2 RST_STREAM with `CANCEL` reason maps to `Code::Cancelled`:
```rust
Some(h2::Reason::CANCEL) => Code::Cancelled,
```
([status.rs L383](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/status.rs?L383))

---

### 2. Application-level mpsc pattern on the server (how `ReceiverStream` enters the picture)

The canonical tonic server streaming pattern, shown in [examples/src/streaming/server.rs L62-L84](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/examples/src/streaming/server.rs?L62-L84) and in [tonic-reflection/src/server.rs L328-L377](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic-reflection/src/server.rs?L328-L377), is:

```rust
let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel(128);
tokio::spawn(async move {
    // producer: calls tx.send(...).await in a loop
    // tx is captured and dropped when the task exits
});
Ok(Response::new(ReceiverStream::new(rx)))
```

`ReceiverStream<T>` ([tokio-stream/src/wrappers/mpsc_bounded.rs L41-L46](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio-stream/src/wrappers/mpsc_bounded.rs?L41-L46)) simply delegates:
```rust
fn poll_next(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Self::Item>> {
    self.inner.poll_recv(cx)
}
```

---

### 3. `mpsc::Receiver::poll_recv` and `None` semantics

**`Receiver::poll_recv`** ([bounded.rs L487-L489](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/bounded.rs?L487-L489)) calls `chan.recv(cx)`.

**`Rx::recv`** ([chan.rs L244-L296](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L244-L296)):

```rust
pub(crate) fn recv(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<T>> {
    // try_recv!() pops from the lock-free queue:
    //   Read::Value(v)  → Ready(Some(v))
    //   Read::Closed    → Ready(None)   ← only when TX_CLOSED is set
    //   None            → continue
    try_recv!();
    self.inner.rx_waker.register_by_ref(cx.waker());
    try_recv!();   // second check after registering waker

    if rx_fields.rx_closed && self.inner.semaphore.is_idle() {
        Ready(None)
    } else {
        Pending          // ← hangs here if neither condition is met
    }
}
```

`Ready(None)` is returned in exactly two cases:
1. The block-level `block.read()` returns `Read::Closed` — which happens only when the slot is not ready **and** `TX_CLOSED` is set ([block.rs L155-L162](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs?L155-L162)).
2. `rx_fields.rx_closed && semaphore.is_idle()` — only reached if the receiver itself called `.close()`.

**`TX_CLOSED` is set only when the last `Tx` clone is dropped.** The `Tx::drop` logic ([chan.rs L208-L220](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L208-L220)):

```rust
impl<T, S> Drop for Tx<T, S> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if self.inner.tx_count.fetch_sub(1, AcqRel) != 1 {
            return;   // ← other clones still alive, early return
        }
        // Only the LAST clone closing reaches here:
        self.inner.tx.close();  // sets TX_CLOSED in the queue block
        self.wake_rx();          // wakes the receiver
    }
}
```

`Tx::clone` ([chan.rs L196-L205](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L196-L205)) increments `tx_count` with `fetch_add(1, Relaxed)`. The channel only signals "closed" to the receiver when `tx_count` reaches zero.

---

### 4. Full cross-repo path: why `Status::cancelled` does not always close the channel

Here is the complete causal chain, with every function responsible:

```
Server emits Status::cancelled
  └─ tonic encodes grpc-status: 1 trailer → sends via h2
  └─ h2 layer sends RST_STREAM CANCEL on the wire

CLIENT SIDE:
  Streaming::poll_next                     [decode.rs L383]
    └─ StreamingInner::poll_data           [decode.rs L233]
         └─ BoxBody::poll_data             (h2 body future)
              └─ h2::RecvStream yields Err(h2::Error, reason=CANCEL)
    └─ map_err: Status::map_error          [decode.rs L126]
         └─ Status::from_error             [status.rs L320]
              └─ Status::from_h2_error     [status.rs L363]
                   └─ code_from_h2: CANCEL → Code::Cancelled [status.rs L383]
    └─ poll_data returns Poll::Ready(Err(Status{Cancelled}))
    └─ poll_next: direction==Response, NOT Request
         → does NOT take the Cancelled short-circuit [decode.rs L237]
         → sets state = State::Error, returns Some(Err(status))
         → stream yields an error item, but does NOT yield None
```

On the **application-level mpsc path** (the `ReceiverStream` pattern):

```
Server spawns task holding mpsc::Sender (tx)
  └─ Task also clones tx for sub-tasks, or tx is captured by closures
       └─ When h2 RST_STREAM arrives, tonic signals no more frames
       └─ The spawned producer task may still be running (blocked on tx.send)
            or has cloned tx elsewhere

  ReceiverStream::poll_next               [mpsc_bounded.rs L44]
    └─ Receiver::poll_recv                [bounded.rs L487]
         └─ Rx::recv                      [chan.rs L244]
              └─ try_recv! → Pending (no message, TX_CLOSED not set)
              └─ registers waker
              └─ rx_closed=false, semaphore not idle
              → returns Poll::Pending      ← HANGS FOREVER
```

**Root cause of the hang:**

`Poll::Pending` is returned — and the receiver stays parked — because `TX_CLOSED` in the mpsc block-level flag ([block.rs L62-L65](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs?L62-L65)) is set only when **every last clone** of the sender has been dropped. `Tx::drop` ([chan.rs L210](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L210)) does an early-return `if tx_count != 1`, so the close signal is never written and `wake_rx()` is never called.

Two concrete scenarios cause an outstanding clone to survive:

| Scenario | Why the clone survives |
|---|---|
| Producer task clones `tx` and passes it to a sub-task or `Arc` | The sub-task/Arc keeps `tx_count > 0`; even after the main task exits, the clone lives on |
| Producer task is blocked on `tx.send().await` waiting for backpressure | The task is parked but `tx` is still alive; the receiver never wakes because `TX_CLOSED` stays unset |

The RST_STREAM from the server does **not** automatically cancel the server-side producer task. Tonic does not inject any cancellation token into the spawned task; the task only notices the client left when `tx.send()` returns `Err(SendError)` (because the response body was dropped). But if the task is blocked inside `tokio::time::sleep`, `tokio::fs::read`, or any other await that isn't `tx.send`, it can stay alive indefinitely — holding its `tx` clone — which keeps `tx_count > 0`, which keeps `TX_CLOSED` unset, which keeps the client's `Receiver::poll_recv` returning `Poll::Pending`, which keeps `Streaming::poll_next` returning `Poll::Pending`, which keeps the client's `.next()` await hanging forever.

---

### Summary table of responsible functions

| Step | Repo | File | Function | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Streaming` body error ingestion | tonic | [decode.rs L126](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L125-L127) | `map_err` / `Status::map_error` | Converts h2 body error to `Status` |
| h2 CANCEL → `Code::Cancelled` | tonic | [status.rs L383](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/status.rs?L372-L389) | `Status::code_from_h2` | Maps `h2::Reason::CANCEL` to `Code::Cancelled` |
| Cancelled not treated as EOF for responses | tonic | [decode.rs L237](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L237-L243) | `StreamingInner::poll_data` | Short-circuit only active for `Direction::Request` |
| `poll_next` drives body | tonic | [decode.rs L383](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L383-L406) | `Streaming::poll_next` | Main polling loop |
| `ReceiverStream` delegates to mpsc | tokio-stream | [mpsc_bounded.rs L44](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio-stream/src/wrappers/mpsc_bounded.rs?L44-L46) | `ReceiverStream::poll_next` | Thin shim over `poll_recv` |
| mpsc receive decision | tokio | [chan.rs L244](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L244-L296) | `Rx::recv` | `Ready(None)` only when `TX_CLOSED` or `rx_closed+idle` |
| Block-level `TX_CLOSED` flag | tokio | [block.rs L62-L65](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs?L62-L65) | `block::read` | Physical flag written by `tx.close()` |
| `TX_CLOSED` written only on last drop | tokio | [chan.rs L208-L219](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L208-L219) | `Tx::drop` | `fetch_sub` early-return if any clone survives |
| Clone increments ref-count | tokio | [chan.rs L196-L205](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L196-L205) | `Tx::clone` | `tx_count.fetch_add(1)` prevents close |

**Fix guidance:** Wrap `tx` in a `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` or use `select!` inside the spawned producer task so that it observes the h2 stream reset and drops its `tx` (and all clones). Alternatively, use `tokio::task::JoinHandle::abort()` when the tonic handler future is dropped, or replace the `spawn + ReceiverStream` pattern with a direct `async_stream::stream!` macro whose future is cancelled when the tonic service drops the response body.
